title: Anandpur Authority Passes to the Khalsa

blocks.text: The poet turns to Anandpur Sahib and says he will only condense what is needed, because the larger Guru-bilas tradition already tells much of the story in detail. (1–3)
At Anandpur Sahib the Guru’s love for the Khalsa grows while wealth, shrines, petitions, and practical authority are increasingly placed into Khalsa hands. (4–6)
This transfer of control enrages masands and hostile officials, who begin whispering that the Guru is making rustic Singhs into rulers and empowering the lowly above established interests. (7–9)
